newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SQUASH-AUSTRALIA WIN WORLD TEAM TITLE DESPITE MARTIN LOSING.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-AUSTRALIA WIN WORLD TEAM TITLE DESPITE MARTIN LOSING.

text.p: Favourites Australia beat England to win the women's world team squash championship on Saturday despite seeing former world open champion Michelle Martin lose the opening encounter of the final.

Martin, who lost the world open title she has held three times when she was ousted in the quarter-finals here by compatriot Liz Irving last week, lost 3-9 9-4 9-4 7-9 7-9 to Cassie Jackman in the team final.
But Irving and Sarah FitzGerald, the woman who replaced Martin as world open champion last week, saved the day for Australia, both winning in straight games.
FitzGerald beat Linda Charman 9-0 9-1 9-3 and Irving defeated Fiona Geaves 9-4 9-4 10-8 to give Australia a 2-1 victory.
To make matters worse for Martin, she suffered a black eye when she was hit by her own racket handle in a collision with Jackman.
The 29-year-old Australian was in bitter mood afterwards. "I am not going to comment on my performance," she said at a post-final news conference.
"Nobody wanted to talk to me when I lost in the world open so I am not going to comment on my individual match here except to say Cassie played very well."
